headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from kotaemon’s document/RAG workflow paired with a non-networked LightZero agent; no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents, PDFs, HTML, MHTML, DOCX, and chat transcripts, so malicious content can be presented as trusted context. LightZero has no documented ingestion path, but if its outputs are copied into kotaemon or a shared workspace is introduced, prompt injection becomes plausible. The pair lacks a documented isolation mechanism, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are pasted into kotaemon prompts or documents
IF both agents are given access to the same workspace or clipboard
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted model output into kotaemon
Add a manual review step before importing LightZero-generated text
Use file naming conventions that mark untrusted inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and broad document types, while LightZero is documented as network-egress none and read/write filesystem false. There is no direct evidence of a shared filesystem, but if kotaemon stores sensitive files in ./ktem_app_data and LightZero is co-located, leakage can occur through operator handling or shared storage. The pairwise path is indirect, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF sensitive documents or API keys are placed in kotaemon’s working directory
IF LightZero is run on the same host with any shared storage or operator-visible logs
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared project folders
Restrict access to ./ktem_app_data
Rotate any API keys exposed to kotaemon
Review host-level permissions before co-locating the agents
requires-engineering: isolate each agent in separate containers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon can run multiple instances and uses broad network egress, while LightZero has no filesystem write, shell, or network egress. Because LightZero cannot modify shared state and kotaemon’s write surfaces are limited to its own app data, direct capability conflict is unlikely. Any conflict would require unusual orchestration or external shared resources.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF kotaemon instances are pointed at the same app-data directory
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid shared git or database targets
Run only one writer per resource
Check for accidental symlinked paths
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon is a customer-support RAG system that can surface citations and generated answers, while LightZero is a game-playing agent with no documented downstream action authority. If LightZero-produced text is fed into kotaemon as authoritative context, kotaemon may render or act on it without verification. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF LightZero output is inserted into kotaemon as source material
IF kotaemon is configured to answer from imported text without human verification
mitigations: Require human review of imported outputs
Label LightZero output as untrusted
Separate generation from retrieval sources
Spot-check citations before publishing
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon handles API keys and customer-support documents, which can include regulated or sensitive data, while LightZero is documented as local-only with no network egress. If the pair is deployed under different retention or residency policies, compliance mismatch can arise even without direct exfiltration. No specific residency regime is documented, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF customer-support documents include regulated personal data
IF kotaemon retention or logging differs from the host policy used for LightZero
mitigations: Confirm retention settings for kotaemon logs
Avoid placing regulated data in shared folders
Document which agent processes which data class
Review API-key handling procedures
requires-engineering: align both agents to one data-handling policy
